key_insight: The paper learns realistic polycrystalline microstructure generation by combining flow matching with a C4-equivariant graph model over anisotropic power diagrams, so rotated inputs yield rotated outputs.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast synthesis of microstructure datasets for materials design and simulation when EBSD data is expensive or unavailable.
method: Represent microstructures as anisotropic power diagrams for a compact geometric encoding.
Train a flow-matching graph neural network with C4 rotational equivariance.
Use training-free guidance to steer samples toward target microstructure styles.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that generated samples can be rendered at arbitrary pixel resolution and that the method is demonstrated on several target microstructure types, including copper weld and 3D-printed stainless steel.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the geometric parametrization and on how well the learned symmetry assumptions match real microstructure variability.
paper_title: $C_4$-Equivariant Flow Matching on Anisotropic Power-Diagram Graphs for Microstructure Generation
